payload.goal:
Add exactly 16 independent warehouse analytics modules to the verified W1 codebase.
Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with a readonly id and project(scenario), where project returns the answer to that module's question.
Each module answers one question, computed from the W1 Scenario, layout and inventory exports:
- src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports the projection "zone-unit-totals": Total units stored in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports the projection "sku-unit-totals": Total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports the projection "bin-occupancy": How many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports the projection "sku-bin-spread": Number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-05.ts exports the projection "zone-sku-mix": Number of distinct SKUs present in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-05.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-06.ts exports the projection "top-bin-by-units": The single bin holding the most units, and how many. Ties break on the lowest bin id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-06.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-07.ts exports the projection "empty-bin-ids": Ids of every bin holding no stock, sorted ascending. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-07.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-08.ts exports the projection "median-occupied-bin-units": Median unit count across bins that hold stock. Even counts average the two middle values. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-08.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-09.ts exports the projection "single-bin-skus": SKUs stored in exactly one bin, sorted ascending. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-09.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-10.ts exports the projection "zone-share-of-units": Each zone's share of total warehouse units, rounded to four decimals, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-10.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-11.ts exports the projection "sku-zone-presence": Zones each SKU appears in, sorted ascending, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-11.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-12.ts exports the projection "occupied-bins-per-zone": Number of bins holding stock in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-12.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-13.ts exports the projection "unit-quantity-extremes": Smallest and largest unit count among bins that hold stock. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-13.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-14.ts exports the projection "top-bin-concentration": Share of total warehouse units held by the single largest bin, rounded to four decimals. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-14.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-15.ts exports the projection "multi-bin-skus": SKUs stored in more than one bin, mapped to their sorted bin ids. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-15.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-16.ts exports the projection "zone-mean-units-per-occupied-bin": Mean units per occupied bin in each zone, rounded to four decimals, keyed by zone id. Zones with no stock report 0. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-16.test.ts.
A module must not import another module; it may import only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Every answer must be derived from the scenario at run time. Do not hardcode results, and do not duplicate the W1 inventory or layout calculations.
Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every module, returning all projections in the order the modules are listed above, with its own tests in src/analytics/registry.test.ts.
Preserve all existing W1 behaviour and checks.
Add a package script named study:wide-graph that writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
Its JSON must be { "schemaVersion": 1, "moduleCount": 16, "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026", "projections": [ { "projectionId": "<the module's projection id>", "value": <that module's answer> }, … ] } with exactly 16 entries in the order the modules are listed above.
Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical JSON.

root.title: Warehouse Analytics Wide Graph
root.objective: Add exactly 16 independent warehouse analytics projections, an ordered registry, focused tests, and a deterministic study:wide-graph JSON command while preserving W1 behavior.
concerns: runtime derivation from W1 scenario, layout, and inventory exports
expectedOutcomes: A shared WarehouseProjection contract exists for the analytics surface.
Exactly sixteen projection modules exist, each independently tested and not importing peer modules.
The registry is the only source module that imports all projection modules and preserves the requested order.
The study:wide-graph script emits the required byte-stable JSON object with sixteen ordered projection entries.
Existing build, typecheck, and W1 tests remain in the configured validation path.

complexitySignals.rationale: Many files are added, but the projection modules are intentionally narrow and independent; the highest integration risk is ordered registry and package script wiring.

cut.rationale: The semantic cut follows independently testable analytics questions, with separate integration leaves for the shared contract, ordered registry, and deterministic command because those concerns have different consumers and acceptance evidence.

expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/contracts.ts exports WarehouseProjection.

The scenario parameter is typed against the W1 scenario surface without embedding layout or inventory calculations.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small file, but it defines the exported interface consumed by all analytics units.

complexitySignals.rationale: Requires both layout bin universe and inventory occupancy, but remains one verifiable answer.

src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts verifies distinct bin counting.

src/analytics/projection-12.test.ts verifies zone-level occupied-bin counts.

complexitySignals.rationale: One occupancy count grouped by layout zone.

children.title: Top Bin Concentration Projection

complexitySignals.rationale: Combines largest-bin selection with exact ratio rounding.

children.title: Multi Bin SKUs Projection

src/analytics/projection-15.test.ts verifies multi-bin filtering and sorted bin-id arrays.

complexitySignals.rationale: One SKU-to-bins classification with deterministic nested ordering.

children.title: Zone Mean Units Per Occupied Bin Projection
children.objective: Implement and test projection-16 for rounded four-decimal mean units per occupied bin per zone, reporting 0 for zones with no stock.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-16.ts exports projection id zone-mean-units-per-occupied-bin.

src/analytics/projection-16.test.ts verifies occupied-bin denominator, four-decimal rounding, and zero-stock zone behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: This projection has the broadest arithmetic edge surface because zone grouping, occupied-bin denominator, rounding, and zero-stock zones all affect acceptance.

children.title: Ordered Analytics Registry
children.objective: Create the sole consumer registry that returns all 16 projections in the requested order, with registry tests.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/registry.ts imports every projection module and is the sole consumer of all modules.
The registry returns all projections in the exact order projection-01 through projection-16.
src/analytics/registry.test.ts verifies count, ids, ordering, and that registry entries conform to WarehouseProjection.

complexitySignals.rationale: The registry crosses all projection modules, but its behavior is limited to sole consumption, conformance, count, and order.
